additional_info.body:
Hi Yunus, Rifki
95/97 chargers (
except uiPwl3 and 5ynz8F)
are updated to v6.1.3 yesterday. Appreciate the support of R&D to do this, especially Benjamin Biedermann to update chargers in short time over weekend.
Upon analyzing the logs of these two chargers, I have an opinion, that this issue has nothing to do with Monta or OCPP running inside the charger.
Monta's expectation is that charger should follow below sequence, which is true
sequence StatusNotification → RemoteStartTransaction → Authorize → StartTransaction → StatusNotification (Charging)
However, please understand that the charger will send
StartTransaction o
nly when there is a successful start of charging i.e. energy transfer or Pilot state getting into “C2” and Charging Phase “
P06 Charge
”.
I have attached logs for charger “
HHSCSk
” and “
qShfXt
” and I will explain, them here.
CHARGER ID - HHSCSk
For Outlet 1, where it is claimed that the charger didn't send the StartTransaction for a session at 11:03 CET, the reason is the failure in the communication between EV and charger and the session never started
2025-03-08T11:03:23 - EV Plugged in DC1: PilotState "A" --> "B2"
2025-03-08T11:03:25 - Charger send StatusNotification “Preparing”
2025-03-08T11:04:57 - For more than a minute there was no Authroization hence the DC1: Charging Phase "P01_AUTHENTICATION" --> "P00_UNKNOWN"
2025-03-08T11:04:59 - DC1: PilotState "B2" --> "E"
2025-03-08T11:05:02 - DC1: PilotState "E" --> "B1"
2025-03-08T11:05:03 - Charger send StatusNotification “Faulted” & then “Preparing”
2025-03-08T11:05:18 - Received OCPP Remote StartTransaction
2025-03-08T11:05:18 - OCPP: Send command: Authorize
2025-03-08T11:09:35 - user unplugs EV DC1: PilotState "B1" --> "A"
Summary : Due to delay in the Authentication the session was failed and hence there was no energy transfer to EV so no StartTransaction. The current SECC SW version doesn't support BEB toggle, hence the later RemoteStartTransaction request has no impact on starting a charging session.
2. The second session on outlet 2 at 2025-03-08T11:11:21 was successful as RemoteStartTransaction was received in time and energy transfer was done. [To Know more, refer attached logs]
CHARGER ID - qShfXt
Query on:
"errorCode":"OtherError"?
"vendorErrorCode":"modbus0 is not connected"?
Charger sends the above Errocode in StatusNotifcation, because there was communication loss with SECC for ~ 750ms., once it was restored the Status was set correctly. see below:
2025-03-09T19:35:32.000447+00:00 [FW060103G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4127] [MBC]  DC1: SECC: no communication for 750ms
OCPP: Send command: StatusNotification (f6c835a6-75fd-41a9-aa8a-bc3a9757a126) - {"connectorId":1,"errorCode":"OtherError","status":"Faulted","vendorId":"SICHARGE D","vendorErrorCode":"modbus0 is not connected"}
OCPP: Send command: StatusNotification (572ac6e7-42e4-463d-b5eb-f61162b778ac) - {"connectorId":1,"errorCode":"NoError","status":"Preparing"}
Kindly note, this message is available in FW v6.1.3 onwards.
Summary from NOC: We don't see any incorrect sequence of OCPP messages being sent by charger to OCPP backend (Monta). The StartTransaction was not send because the charging session was not initiated due to failed communication with EV mainly because of delay in Authorization after an EV was plugged in.
I my opinion updating to v6.1.3 will help or support here, because it has same SECC FW version as in v6.0.3 and that doesn't support BEB toggle. @michele, correct me if I am wrong here.
P.S.: I have marked the R&D colleagues and CS head in Bcc of this email to summarize the findings and update the progress. I will request all to follow the conversation here in ISP to track the issue with transparency and close other email conversations.
Feel free to give me a call if you need further clarifications.
Thank you.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0411427-DC/Si-D/TR-[Y2/S3 300000004078] Charging Issues with Monta CRM:01811000714
additional_info.body:
Hello Daniel,
Please find my answers to your questions below :
Is this happening only with a certain vehicle type?
[RS]: No
Are we sure this is not a Monta configuration after-all? There is a parameter in OCPP, ConnectionTimeOut, which determines how much time the driver has to plug the vehicle in before the transaction times out. Could it be that the parameter set by Monta is different (lower) than the parameter set by the previous backend, and this is triggering the issue? Still could indicate a vehicle compatibility issue, not a Monta issue, but changing this parameter could be the band-aid we need.
[RS]: Prima facia, it doesn't appear to be a configuration issue. But yes, the OCPP parameter ConnectionTimeOut can be increased to before the session times out. This has been set to 180 Sec, however this will only support user if they Authorize first and connect EV later. However the sessions I have analyzed so far has user plugging in EV first and Authorizing later, in this scenario the EV-EVSE communication start and goes to “Authentication” Stage as per ISO 15118 and here we have 59 sec timeouts as per standard. So it's a BEB toggeling case.
If there is a delay in authorization sent by Monta to the charger compared to the previous backend, then this is for sure, 100%, a Monta issue. Please confirm
[RS]: May be, it can also be because of user (delay in scanning App or initiating RemoteStartTransaction) or can be from Monta Backend. Still to be analyzed.
We have received additional inputs from Emre, I will keep you in the conversations.
Thank you.
With best regards,

Hello Emre,
I am following up on our conversation via Teams and summarizing the findings from today's analysis in written form.
I am referring to the analysis on charger
qShfXt
, as per the attached email. According to the criteria that Monta uses to calculate failed sessions, they consider a session failed if it starts with a “RemoteStartTransaction” and “Authorize” command but does not receive a “StartTransaction”.
How does this reflect on our charger? Since the “StartTransaction” is sent from the charger to the Backend only when the current flow begins (Charging Phase P06_Charge), whatever happens in the meantime is considered by Monta as a failed session. This includes issues with the charger, failures during CableCheck, issues with the EV, and improper conduct by the end user.
Below are the details of the cases analyzed today:
Case 1:
It was reported a failed session today (17.03.2025). In the logs you can see that:
- DC2 is plugged in.
2025-03-17T13:34:37.728173+00:00 [FW060103G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4127] [DCC] DC2: PilotState "A" --> "B2"

{
"connectorId":
1
,

}
This is clearly an example of improper conduct of the end user, which results into a failed session considered by Monta.
Case 2:
Session failed on DC1 on 2025-03-16T10:15:07. In this case, I noticed a wrong behavior of the charger during CableCheck and PreCharge phase. I can see how the TF1 voltage transducer detects some voltage on the outlet since the moment of plug in (the voltage transducer is connected after the OutGoingCoil contactor, so it measures the voltage on the cable/plug). During CableCheck and PreCharge, the voltage looks oscillating, and the session fails because the charegr is not able to build the voltage during pre-charge within the precharge timeout.
I believe that in this case we are having an HW issue in the charger.
As per agreed via call, please open another ticket specifically for this charger, so not to mix the topics.
Action items for this specific charger:
The issue could be either in the TDK contactor QA21-22, or in the Voltage transducer TF1 and the connection in XD10.1A.
Next step is to monitor remotely the charger via debug station during charging sessions on DC1.
Goal is to see if we have voltage drops or not. This analysis could distinct between a TDK issue or a TF1/XD10.1A issue.

At first glance, it looks like the session didn't start due to an action from the EV, which resulted in a communication error between EV and Charger.

Good evening colleagues,
Today I had an alignment with Emre, and we jointly agreed to close this ticket and the escalation from Monta and Borusan EnBW.
Over the past months, Siemens HQ supported the colleagues from Turkey to face the escalation coming from client Borusan EnBW. Several topics were addressed and supported from Siemens service and R&D side:
Analysis of claimed increase of charging failure rate from Monta.
®
Identified that no increase in charging failure rate happened, just the onboarding of Monta on the Borusan chargers and the notice of a high failure rate.
Analysis of the
high failure rate of charging session due to “Start Transaction Timeout” claimed by Monta.
®
clarified that
Monta reported as failed sessions all the sessions failing between Authorization and actual Charging. This criterion includes all possible scenarios of failure: issues on the charger, issues on the EVs, communication issues between EV and charger, improper conduct by the end customer in using the charger, authorization timeout, etc.
Because of this broad scenario, specific failure patterns have been identified, excluded and mitigated.
®
Supported Monta to identify issues on the transmitted data from Backend and issues between Backend and App provider.
Mitigation form Service and R&D side consisted in supporting the fleet with FW updates to the most stable version, and installation of EcoG HotFix v1.4.11.
The Hotfix provided clear benefits to the fleet, such as an increase of the Authorization Timeout form EcoG point of view.
High failure rate with TOGG EVs.
®
Analyzed logs and fleet behavior. Found out that the high failure rate with TOGG EVs is due to issues from the EV side.
RC-TR and R&D, together with EcoG, supported the communication towards TOGG.
®
TOGG stated that they are running an update to overcome the issues.
At this stage, no further topics are pending on Siemens' side, from either service or R&D side, and this has been the case for over a month.
Therefore, it has been mutually decided to close the ticket and the escalation. For any future issues related to the Borusan EnBW chargers, it was agreed to follow the standard process by opening tickets on ISP, per issue or per charger.
